title: Improve wear-resistant ability of laser-cladded medium manganese steel coatings:Effects of TRIP/TWIP mechanism
abstract: The strain hardening mechanisms of medium manganese steel (MMS) mainly include twin-induced plasticity (TWIP) and phase transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) synergistic strengthening and single TRIP strengthening. The differences in wear resistance performance resulting from the strengthening effects of these two mechanisms under wear conditions still lack clear understanding. This study investigates how the dilution rate influences the wear resistance of laser-cladded MMS coatings by regulating their deformation hardening mechanisms. Two types of MMS coatings with different dilution rates were prepared using laser cladding on 16Mn steel substrates: a low-dilution-rate coating (LDR-MMS, ∼17.3%) and a high-dilution-rate coating (HDR-MMS, ∼25.5%). The microstructure, phase composition, and grain morphology were characterized by XRD, EBSD, and SEM. Dry sliding wear tests were conducted under a load of 200 N for different durations (15, 30, and 45 min) to evaluate wear resistance. The work-hardening mechanisms were further analyzed by TEM and stacking fault energy (SFE) calculations. The major observations are as follows: LDR-MMS consists mainly of austenite and TiC, while HDR-MMS additionally contains initial martensite (IM) and cementite due to reduced austenite stability caused by lower C and Mn contents. During wear, LDR-MMS exhibits a synergistic TRIP + TWIP effect, forming a continuous hardened layer with a volume loss of only 0.73 × 10−2 mm3 in the later wear stage. In contrast, HDR-MMS relies on a single TRIP effect, and the interface between IM and stress-induced martensite (SIM) leads to crack initiation and hardened layer spalling, resulting in a significantly higher volume loss of 2.83 × 10−2 mm3. These results demonstrate that controlling the dilution rate effectively tailors the deformation hardening mechanism and wear performance of MMS coatings, providing a theoretical basis for process optimization. This study elucidated the regulatory mechanism of dilution rate on the microstructure and wear resistance of MMS coatings, providing a theoretical basis for the optimization of coating processes and the precise regulation of deformation hardening mechanisms.
